title: Pilot go-decision matrix and cutover responsibilities
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on final go/no-go decision matrix, defining cutover responsibilities, canary thresholds, A/B split plan, and monitoring/runbook handoff. Agreement to run a dry-run on 2026-06-26, Redwood to deliver updated runbook and dashboard links. Next step: pricing + commitment conversation after successful dry-run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Martinez, Priya Nair (Redwood); Jordan Li, Maya Thompson, Samir Patel (AstraFold)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Final pilot checks, decide go/no-go gating, agree runbook owners and dry-run schedule.

00:00 Alex: okay everyone uh thanks for joining i think we have about 50 minutes, i'll kick off. quick agenda - walk through the decision matrix, owners for the cutover runbook, canary thresholds, monitoring, then decide dry-run date.
00:18 Jordan: yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it. we're heads down on the last integration bits, a few questions on traffic shaping and the kv cache warmup.
00:30 Priya: great, i'll cover kv cache warmup and the auto-prefix cache thing, we have a small warmup job that primes the caches to avoid initial latency spikes. sometimes the transcription says K-V cash which is fun but yes it's K-V cache.
00:47 Maya: quick context - our SLA goal is 99.9 for p95 response under normal load, our internal perf tests show we're hitting p95 around 220ms on the hosted variant but with dedicated we saw mid 140s in your benchmarks.
01:05 Alex: right, and that matches the model families we suggested. for the pilot we default to the dedicated pool with fallback to hosted for burst traffic, unless you prefer routing by cost.
01:22 Jordan: we prefer predictable latency so dedicated makes sense. one of our concerns is canary thresholds - what metrics should we gate on? latency, error rate, and quality spike?
01:40 Priya: recommended three-tier gate: latency (p95 > 300ms is fail), error rate (5xx > 0.5% over 5 minutes is fail), and quality/regression check (sampled prompts with human raters or automatic eval; if top-level metric drops by more than 3% compared to baseline fail). note that automatic eval can be noisy, so we'll bias to manual review for first canary.
02:05 Samir: for the error rate threshold - is 0.5% tight for our traffic volume? at peak 50 RPS that's like, what, a few errors. we want to avoid false positives during transient spikes.
02:20 Priya: good point - we recommend a rolling window and a secondary tier - orange threshold at 1% triggers slower ramp but doesn't abort, red threshold at 2% aborts immediate. so a graduated approach.
02:38 Maya: can you repeat the ramp steps for an A/B test? we want to start small and double every 10 minutes?
02:45 Alex: our suggestion: A/B staged ramp - 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. timing can be 10-15 minutes between steps and each step needs green checks from the three gates. if a gate trips we hold and investigate for up to 30 minutes then decide rollback.
03:10 Jordan: sounds sensible. who's on call to make the go/no-go decision during quiet window? we need named owners.
03:20 Alex: proposal: Redwood SE (Priya) monitors infra and model-side metrics, AstraFold SRE (Samir) owns service telemetry and rollback triggers, Jordan as project lead makes the final go/no-go with input from Maya for quality. we can put this in the runbook.
03:40 Samir: ok, i'll take the SRE lead. Priya, you'll run the model dashboards. Jordan, you want me to ping you at each ramp step or only for anomalies?
03:50 Jordan: ping at each ramp step and for anomalies, please. that's our preference.
04:00 Priya: we'll add Slack hooks and a dedicated channel for the cutover. also add an on-call rotation if this moves to production.
04:13 Maya: monitoring - what dashboards will you hand over? we need per-route p50/p95/p99, token counts, model memory, KV hit rate, and cost-per-request estimates.
04:25 Priya: yes we'll provide a dashboard template: latency, error rate, throughput, KV hit rate, GPU utilization, and sampling of outputs for quality. links will be in the runbook. Redwood will maintain the dashboard during pilot; after launch we will hand over a view-only link and the alert rules.
04:45 Jordan: about data residency and logs - AstraFold needs request logs retained for 90 days and we need SOC2 paperwork for audit.
04:55 Alex: Redwood is SOC2 compliant and we can enable longer audit retention as an add-on. for private deployment customers we also support VPC peering and KMS integration for key management.
05:10 Maya: one more legal note - PII redaction is required for a subset of our payloads. is there an easy way to do that?
05:20 Priya: we have pre-processing hooks and can support a redaction layer client-side or via the gateway. we'll add an example sanitizer snippet to the runbook.
05:35 Jordan: can we run a dry-run with traffic mirroring first before any user-visible switch?
05:42 Alex: absolutely - traffic mirroring for a baseline run is low risk. suggested plan: mirroring for 24 hours, then a scheduled dry-run where we do a full staged ramp against a canary slice, then the actual cutover next week if green.
06:05 Samir: timeline? we want the production cutover by end of next week if possible.
06:12 Alex: proposed schedule - mirroring 2026-06-25 02:00 UTC for 24 hours, dry-run 2026-06-26 03:00 UTC (quiet window), final cutover 2026-07-01 03:00 UTC (quiet window). does that work?
06:28 Maya: the 03:00 UTC quiet window is fine for our global team.
06:35 Jordan: ok confirm the mirroring and dry-run. we will need the runbook and the dashboard links before the dry-run.
06:42 Priya: Redwood will deliver updated runbook by 2026-06-26 00:00 UTC (so you have it before dry-run) and dashboard links by 2026-06-25 18:00 UTC.
06:52 Alex: i'll also share the pricing impact of routing fallback to hosted for bursts by EOD tomorrow.
07:00 Jordan: now let's talk rollback scenarios - full rollback vs degrade-to-hosted fallback. which do you recommend?
07:12 Priya: for user-facing apps we recommend degrade-to-hosted fallback (graceful degradation) where we route a percentage to hosted variant automatically if canary triggers. full rollback is heavier and requires state reconciliation for KV cache; that'll be fallback plan B.
07:30 Samir: for cache state - if we rollback, how do we ensure correctness? we have ephemeral session tokens stored in Redis.
07:38 Priya: we advise session reconciliation scripts in the runbook and a KV cache priming step before traffic flip. we'll include the exact commands.
07:50 Maya: alerting - who gets paged for what thresholds? Samir to page infra, Priya to page model/SE, Alex to page AE for stakeholder updates?
08:02 Alex: yes that's fine. we'll codify escalation matrix.
08:10 Jordan: are there any blockers from Redwood side for the dry-run?
08:15 Priya: no blockers, we have capacity reserved. need the final route definitions and example payloads from your side to prime KV cache.
08:28 Jordan: action - Maya to share route list and sample payloads by 2026-06-24 EOD.
08:35 Maya: yes will do.
08:40 Jordan: next topic - evaluation / quality checks during canary. do you have a sample prompt set?
08:46 Priya: we'll share the canary prompt set and automatic eval harness. for first canary we want human spot checks of 50 samples every ramp step.
09:00 Maya: okay that sounds manageable.
09:06 Jordan: security review - any extra steps for KMS? we use AWS KMS and need CMK usage logs forwarded to our SIEM.
09:15 Alex: Redwood supports AWS KMS integration and can configure audit log forwarding to your SIEM via our log exporter. we'll include the config snippet in the runbook.
09:28 Samir: what about rate limiting - do you have per-customer quotas? during pilot we might burst beyond expected.
09:35 Priya: we have per-api-key rate limits and can set soft quotas during pilot to avoid throttling. we can also configure graceful 429 handling and retries.
09:48 Maya: regression alerting - if quality drops but latency is fine, what's the recommended action?
09:55 Priya: pause ramp and escalate to human review; if the drop is persistent beyond 15 minutes rollback or route back to previous model.
10:08 Jordan: ok good. any risks you want to call out?
10:12 Alex: main risks - cache warmup causing initial latency spike, noisy automatic eval false positives, and insufficient observability on token-level cost. mitigation: dry-run mirroring, manual review for first canary, and token-level dashboard.
10:30 Maya: question - can we enable verbose sampling for the dry-run to capture edge cases?
10:35 Priya: yes we'll enable increased sampling and redact PII as per the sanitizer.
10:42 Jordan: timeline recap?
10:45 Alex: mirroring starts 2026-06-25 02:00 UTC; runbook by 2026-06-26 00:00 UTC; dry-run 2026-06-26 03:00 UTC; final cutover target 2026-07-01 03:00 UTC.
10:58 Maya: agreed.
11:05 Jordan: any ask on pricing?
11:10 Alex: i'll share hosted fallback cost delta and a proposed reserved capacity delta for dedicated by tomorrow EOD.
11:20 Samir: we may need a short SLO clause in the pilot contract for response time guarantees during the quiet window.
11:28 Alex: Redwood legal can draft a 2-week pilot SLO guarantee; i'll loop in sales ops after this call.
11:40 Maya: final check - do we have a checklist for pre-cutover smoke tests?
11:45 Priya: yes we'll include smoke tests: basic end-to-end, latency/throughput at ramp steps, KV hit rate check, sample qualitative checks.
11:58 Jordan: perfect. i think that's everything.
12:03 Alex: great recap - i'll list owners and action items in the runbook. any final comments?
12:10 Maya: none from me.
12:12 Jordan: no, thanks everyone.
12:15 Alex: thanks all, we will reconvene after dry-run results.

Questions (logged):
- How do we handle PII redaction in sampled payloads? (answered: pre-processing hooks and sanitizer examples included)
- What's the exact error threshold logic? (answered: rolling window + orange/red tiers)

Action items (brief):
- Maya Thompson: share route list and sample payloads by 2026-06-24 EOD
- Priya Nair (Redwood): deliver updated runbook by 2026-06-26 00:00 UTC and dashboard links by 2026-06-25 18:00 UTC
- Alex Martinez: share pricing delta for hosted fallback by 2026-06-25 EOD
- Jordan Li: confirm quiet window schedule and reviewer list by 2026-06-25 12:00 UTC

End of transcript.
